subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment In the given sentence.**

I will not go out if __is raining. __
solution:
The correct answer is: **It rains**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the present tense.
 
• The correct option also uses the present tense but replaces "**is**" with "**it**".
 
• "**It**" is a pronoun that refers to the rain.
 
• This sentence means that the speaker will only go out if it's not raining.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Corrected sentence**:* I will not go out if it rains.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**raining**" is a present participle, which can be used as a verb or adjective, but it does not fit in this sentence as the main verb.
 
• "**will rain**" is in the future tense, which changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
• "**rained**" is in the past tense, which also changes the meaning of the sentence.
